items.q: Well young woman with platelets 22, large platelets on film, normal haemoglobin and white cells and gum bleeding most likely has what?
items.exp: Isolated immune platelet destruction with compensatory large platelets and no other cytopenia or sickness is ITP, a diagnosis of exclusion after film review excludes schistocytes, blasts and clumping artefact.
r: Incorrect. Aplasia lowers all three lines with empty marrow.
Correct. Isolated destruction pattern means ITP.
Incorrect. DIC sickens with clotting consumption and schistocytes.
Incorrect. Leukaemia floods film with blasts and other cytopenias.
items.kp: One line down, big platelets, well patient: ITP.

items.q: Palpable purpura on buttocks and legs with arthritis, abdominal pain and haematuria in a child indicates which vasculitis?
items.exp: IgA vasculitis deposits IgA in small vessels causing palpable purpura (buttocks, extensor legs), arthralgia, gut colic or intussusception and IgA nephritis needing urine surveillance for years.
r: Incorrect. Polyarteritis affects medium arteries with aneurysms, sparing this pattern.
Correct. Childhood palpable purpura tetrad means IgA vasculitis.
Incorrect. GPA centres upper airway lung kidney granulomas.
Incorrect. TTP causes flat petechiae with microangiopathy chaos.
items.kp: Palpable plus IgA in a child: follow the urine for years.

items.q: Absent platelet aggregation to all agonists except ristocetin with normal platelet size indicates which receptor defect?
items.exp: Glanzmann platelets adhere via intact GPIb ristocetin pathway but cannot aggregate without fibrinogen receptor IIb IIIa, causing lifelong mucocutaneous bleeding with absent clot retraction.
r: Incorrect. Bernard Soulier fails ristocetin adhesion with giant platelets.
Correct. Aggregation receptor loss means Glanzmann disease.
Incorrect. Storage defects show second wave release failure milder.
Incorrect. Severe vWD fails ristocetin cofactor activity.
items.kp: Adhesion intact, aggregation absent: Glanzmann IIb IIIa.

items.q: Giant platelets, mild thrombocytopenia and failed ristocetin adhesion indicate which defect?
o: Bernard Soulier syndrome (GPIb IX V loss)
items.exp: Bernard Soulier lacks the von Willebrand adhesion receptor complex, producing giant platelets that cannot tether under shear, with variable thrombocytopenia from defective production.
r: Incorrect. Glanzmann platelets are normal sized aggregating failures.
Correct. Giant platelets failing ristocetin mean Bernard Soulier.
Incorrect. ITP platelets are large young but receptors intact.
Incorrect. May Hegglin giants carry Dohle like inclusions differently.
items.kp: Giant plus cannot stick equals Bernard Soulier.

items.q: Aspirin antiplatelet action lasts how long after one dose and why?
o: Platelet lifespan (about 7 to 10 days), irreversible COX acetylation in anucleate platelets
items.exp: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet cyclo oxygenase, and anucleate platelets cannot synthesise replacement enzyme, so thromboxane suppression lasts the platelet lifespan with daily ten percent recovery from new platelets.
r: Incorrect. NSAID non aspirin binding is reversible and brief.
Correct. Irreversible hit for the platelet life span.
Incorrect. New platelets restore function within days.
Incorrect. Excretion speed does not govern platelet recovery.
items.kp: One aspirin silences each platelet for its whole life.

items.q: Childhood ITP after viral illness most often follows which course?
o: Spontaneous remission within weeks to months in most children
items.exp: Acute childhood ITP (post viral, abrupt petechiae) remits spontaneously in the majority within six months, managed by bleeding severity more than count alone, unlike chronic adult disease.
r: Incorrect. Chronicity defines a minority childhood course.
Correct. Most childhood ITP self resolves.
Incorrect. Marrow failure is a different disease excluded at diagnosis.
Incorrect. Leukaemia is excluded by film, not a progression.
items.kp: Child ITP usually burns out; adult ITP usually stays.

items.q: Pseudothrombocytopenia (falsely low automated count) is classically caused by what artefact?
o: Platelet clumping in EDTA anticoagulant, normal on citrate film
items.exp: EDTA dependent antibodies clump platelets in vitro fooling counters while the patient has no bleeding; smear review and citrate recount expose artefact before any treatment error.
r: Correct. EDTA clumping fakes low counts.
Incorrect. Destruction lowers true counts with bleeding risk.
Incorrect. Dilution lowers all parameters proportionally mildly.
Incorrect. Cold agglutinins clump red cells, a different artefact.
items.kp: Low count, no bleeding: look at the film for clumps first.

items.q: Uraemic platelet dysfunction bleeding is best reversed acutely by which measures among these principles?
o: Platelet transfusion as sole lasting fix
Dialysis optimisation and desmopressin (correcting uraemic milieu)
items.exp: Uraemic toxins reversibly poison platelet adhesion and granule function, so dialysis, desmopressin (endothelial vWF release), anaemia correction and conjugated oestrogens improve haemostasis; transfused platelets are poisoned too.
r: Incorrect. Transfused platelets dysfunction in same milieu quickly.
Correct. Clean the milieu and release von Willebrand factor.
Incorrect. Spleen removal does not fix uraemic function.
Incorrect. Warfarin concerns factors, not uraemic platelets.
items.kp: Uraemic bleeding is environmental: fix the milieu, not just add platelets.

items.q: Heparin induced thrombocytopenia paradoxically causes which feared complication needing heparin cessation?
o: Arterial and venous thrombosis from platelet factor 4 antibody activation
items.exp: HIT antibodies against PF4 heparin complexes activate platelets causing thrombocytopenia with thrombosis (limb, adrenal, cerebral) five to ten days after exposure, treated by stopping heparin and non heparin anticoagulation, never platelet transfusion routinely.
r: Incorrect. Bleeding is not the paradoxical danger.
Correct. Low platelets clotting widely means HIT.
Incorrect. Marrow remains productive in HIT.
Incorrect. Haemolysis is not the defining mechanism.
items.kp: Falling platelets on heparin plus new clot equals HIT. Stop heparin.

items.q: Senile purpura on forearms in elderly patients results from what vessel support failure?
o: Dermal collagen and elastic atrophy losing perivascular support from ageing and sun
items.exp: Age and actinic damage thin dermis and perivascular collagen so minor trauma tears unsupported vessels into large flat ecchymoses on extensor forearms with normal platelets and clotting, reassuring without extensive workup when typical.
r: Incorrect. Counts are normal in senile purpura.
Correct. Lost dermal support tears vessels benignly.
Incorrect. IgA purpura is palpable inflammatory childhood disease.
Incorrect. Factor XIII causes deep delayed wound bleeding.
items.kp: Elderly forearm bruises with normal tests: support failure, not disease hunt.
